label: Truthmaker doctrine described and…: Every true claim has some entity that makes it true
term: Truthmaker doctrine described and rejected by Merricks
definition: Every true claim has some entity that makes it true. Merricks defines this doctrine and rejects it, retaining a necessity demand only for mere-existence truths. This source description does not itself quantify over formal worlds or identify all truthmakers with existence-label reasons.
note: Selected-world encoding of the doctrine content only: for each true represented claim there exists a maker, with no shared witness required. No all-world policy, soundness, actual-existence conjunct or existence-label restriction is added. Making remains a primitive substantive relation; the legitimacy of its grounding/aboutness interpretation and completeness of the represented claim and eligible-maker domains remain OPEN. Source reporting and rejection are metadata, not propositions proved by this declaration.
